policy.reference_syntax: An origin or basis_ref is source_alias followed by # and an RFC 6901 JSON pointer. Resolve source_alias through sources, verify its complete-file SHA256, then resolve the pointer.
policy.lossless_originals: Every accounting row preserves the source group's ordered member_ids as members. Each complete unchanged original is sources[origin alias]#/raw_findings/<member ID>. The complete source group at origin also retains its original classes, evidence references and consolidation reasons. No source field is rewritten or discarded.
policy.retained_canonical_id: For new_AB and C_blocked accounting rows, the canonical ID remains the row's id. No raw ID is split or counted twice.
policy.neutral_claim_resolution: Each claims object contains exactly id, claim, file, line. claim, file and line are copied exactly from the canonical raw_findings[id] object, not from a reference object or a paraphrased group summary.
policy.eligibility: new_AB denotes a pure original A/B proposal packaged for subsequent handling, not a confirmed defect, acceptance, fix approval or completed countercheck. No behavior was reviewed here.
policy.C_rule: Any new group with an original C proposal is C_blocked, including the four mixed B/C groups listed below. C_blocked groups are excluded from claims and receive neither fix approval nor automatic countercheck approval.
policy.external_C_rule: All existing original-C restrictions and the eight additionally referenced existing C blocks remain blocked. Related new A/B proposals cannot upgrade them or inherit their status.
policy.equivalence_rule: Merge only an equivalent complete claim with the same entry, expected contract and material failure scenario. A shared file, helper, symptom or partial overlapping component is insufficient. Preserve differences and leave uncertain overlaps open.
policy.existing_links: The five links already present in the inputs remain existing links. They are never counted as new claims. Their canonical targets are unchanged; no earlier judgments, reasons, votes or acceptance decisions are copied into this artifact.
policy.coverage_limit: Declared primary intervals are reported complete by the inputs. That is not proof of actual full source reading, error freedom or behavioral correctness. The upstream transcript/model audit reported by the task was not repeated here.
policy.execution_limit: No application source changes, runtime probes, tests, builds, Git mutations, browser work, additional reviewers, delegation or session messages. Only this artifact is written.

comparison.method: Compare the bound canonical claim inventory, unchanged new member originals and selectively resolved original scenarios/evidence of close alternatives. Text similarity was used only to locate alternatives, never as an equivalence decision or a claims cutoff. Full source transcripts and the primary manifest were not loaded.
comparison.result: No additional equivalent complete group was established. Keep all 90 pure A/B proposal IDs canonical, all 36 new C groups blocked and the five preexisting links separate. This is not a global uniqueness claim outside the bound artifacts.

mixed_BC_C_blocks.reason: The quota group contains original C and B proposals. Keep the complete quota originals and their reasons unchanged; the group remains conservatively C.
Publisher authentication rejection has conflicting original B/C proposals. Preserve both originals and keep the group conservatively C.
Business-effect durability has conflicting original B/C proposals. Preserve the interrupted-update scenarios and keep the group conservatively C.
Owner cancellation has conflicting original B/C proposals. Preserve all four originals, including retained fingerprints, and keep the group conservatively C.

external_C_blocks.status: All 58 remain blocked; references preserve restrictions only, not reviewer judgments or votes. None enters claims.

already_linked_groups.basis: Both originals describe the same affiliate callback accepting an attacker-authorized fresh code/state in a victim browser and issuing the attacker's affiliate session without initiating-browser binding.
The originals match the existing login-reassignment account/profile/credit-note/Stripe ownership contract. They do not expand that link to the separately retained portal financial-ledger claim.
Same oversized expires_in conversion panic in the detached proactive Kick/YouTube refresh task, stopping later scheduled refreshes until restart; not the separate callback panic.
Same proactive scheduler counting an absent-provider-client no-op as a renewal despite unchanged stored credentials.
Same completed provider-refresh failure discarded by the batch loop without diagnostics. The existing original C qualification remains in force.

related_not_equivalent.reason: Recycled-login identity is shared, but affiliate portal ledger reads, profile/document/payout ownership, Stripe portal, billing profile, monetization and historical analytics have distinct entry and data-access contracts. Preserve every separate group; the existing affiliate link covers only its original ownership contract.

Sequential email-only PII creation preventing migration, a partial-save snapshot reverting a profile update and a stale global migration selection overwriting a later save are different scenarios despite the shared PII saver.
Affiliate callback scheme construction, dashboard OAuth validation, Discord host comparison, health-probe validation and CSRF comparison are distinct IPv6 contracts, not one duplicated claim.

Affiliate is_active toggles act on affiliate accounts. Streamer archive/block toggles act on independent partner state and separately implemented paths. The read-modify-write pattern alone is not equivalence.

Swallowed errors occur at different session, account, statistics, contest-alias, chatter-session and observability reads. Their failure inputs and authorization, attribution or successful-response contracts differ.
An unordered initial lookup selecting inactive history differs from a final visibility check validating another Twitch identity with the same local revision.

Submission quota bypass, own-clip vote acceptance and deterministic slot collision after rebinding require different persistence contracts. The older link-callback swap deadlock does not establish any of those post-link failures. The mixed quota group stays C.
An SQL roadmap timestamp marking an unseen private feedback reply read differs from JSON roadmap file overwrite loss or corruption.

Camera row resurrection, registration after revocation, replacement-publisher self-revocation, failed revoke persistence and failed initial consent persistence have different orderings and expected transitions.

Authentication rejection retaining capture, network failure disabling retry and pending device acquisition restarting capture after Stop are distinct paths. The authentication-rejection group remains C.

A failed concurrent refresh overwriting a successful refresh differs from retaining an ordinary failed refresh for six hours. Do not promote the C failure-retention group using the B concurrent-publication proposal.
A one-shot callback panic after consuming OAuth state differs from termination of the unsupervised recurring refresh task. The latter's preexisting link does not absorb the callback proposal.
Platform connection state, dashboard session/OAuth state and Steam-link request retention have different producers and cleanup ownership. Each C restriction is preserved.

Platform-account linking CSRF, a Social Studio/Uplink state-and-principal collision, affiliate login CSRF, Discord admin completion and partner-token login have different initiating principals and entry contracts.

EventSub ingress MessageId durability, post-lease business-effect guard durability and internal HTTP idempotency OwnerSlot cancellation are independent namespaces and persistence contracts. The two mixed-C groups remain blocked.

OfflineThrottle suppressing a failed retry, ignored session-finalization failure, replay of an already completed online job and reversed initial batch delivery are distinct transitions and ordering failures.

Create/revoke races, preservation of disabled subscriptions, old-callback cleanup untracking a live twin, authentic repeated revocation and tampering with an unsigned message-type header have different inputs and bookkeeping contracts.
Comma-truncation of a parsed Origin hostname and treating an unrepresentable Origin header as absent are different validation mechanisms, even in the same guard.
Stale-owner completion, timeout publication to waiters, owner cancellation and retained full-body fingerprints are separate idempotency lifecycle/resource contracts. The cancellation group remains C.
Ignoring DSN query overrides causes false identity agreement; rereading untrimmed configuration causes false mismatch. Sharing fingerprint code does not make their scenarios equivalent.

Internal legacy fallback and dashboard public fallback use separate entrances, clients and body-size/timeout contracts. Similar buffering or pre-upstream body waits do not transfer classification or establish a complete duplicate.

Affiliate reads, profile reads, onboarding writes, contest finalization, feedback locks, overlay identity reads, token snapshots, EventSub handlers, inbox confirmation, poller diagnostics, discord-flag reads, verification locks and the older dashboard operations stall distinct operations or pools/loops. An absent-deadline theme is not an equivalent request contract. All C blocks, especially the existing limiter block, remain unchanged.

unresolved_overlaps.reason: The verify-promotion interleaving overlaps exactly in part, but the concurrency original also asserts independent history-reactivation ingress. Complete groups are not coextensive. Keep both canonical and unsplit; no equivalence or redundant whole-group count is asserted.

Both include crash-before-core-inbox-persistence, but the second additionally asserts a simultaneous duplicate acknowledged while the first attempt is pending and transactional channel.subscription.end. These added scenarios/writer contracts prevent a lossless complete-group link. Keep both canonical.

Internal lifecycle and dashboard analytics lifecycle are separately implemented twins. Internal removal retry returns success/not stored, dashboard removal retries return a fallback success or 404; stale Discord-ID and membership/profile writers also differ. Keep all entry contracts separate. A coordinated future correction scope cannot be inferred from matching helper shapes.

Internal healthz fingerprint production and two dashboard fingerprint consumers share query-override omissions but have independent implementations and entries. The cross-service normalization contract remains open; do not collapse the claims or upgrade DA05's existing C qualification.

The original cites an internal-home AvatarCache retention pattern, but no corresponding canonical group occurs in the bound W02/DA03/DA04/DA05/DA06 or five new inventories. Do not invent a counterpart ID or an equivalence. The new profile-cache group remains C.

The original cites social-media pagination offset twins outside the bound inventories. No exact counterpart group is available here. Keep the commission contract canonical and do not link it merely by unchecked arithmetic shape.

context_limits.reason: The input records one absent context-only legacy reference. It is not an unread primary interval, not assumed legacy behavior and not a consolidation blocker.

The complete hash-bound original objects remain authoritative for every group, including broader noncanonical member scenarios. Neutral claim text is only the canonical original's claim; it does not replace those originals or narrow their accounting.
